t.1.148.1: Kuntī said: I wish to know truly what the root of this sorrow is. Having learned it, I would remove it, if it is possible to remove.
t.1.148.2: What you say, O lady rich in austerity, befits the virtuous; but this sorrow cannot be removed by any human being.
t.1.148.3: Near this city dwells a rākṣasa named Baka, a being of great strength, who is lord of this country and of the city.
t.1.148.4: Fattened on human flesh, that evil-minded man-eater, a mighty king of the Asuras, constantly guards this land.
t.1.148.5: Endowed with the might of a rākṣasa, he guards both the city and the country; because of him we have no fear of enemy armies or of other beings.
t.1.148.6: The wage fixed for him is a meal of a cartload of rice, two buffaloes, and one man who takes it and goes to him.
t.1.148.7: Each man in his turn provides that meal; that turn comes round only after many years, yet men find it impossible to escape.
t.1.148.8: And whatever men at any time strive for deliverance from it, that Rākṣasa kills them along with their sons and wives and devours them.
t.1.148.9: The king here in Vetrakīyagṛha has not adopted the policy by which lasting well-being might now be secured for this people.
t.1.148.10: Surely we deserve this, we who dwell in the realm of a weak ruler, ever anxious, having taken refuge with a bad king.
t.1.148.11: To whom are brahmins answerable, or at whose will do they move about? For it is by virtues that they are made to dwell in a place, like birds that roam wherever they wish.
t.1.148.12: One should first secure a king, then a wife, then wealth; and when this triad has been gathered, one may support one's kinsmen and sons.
t.1.148.13: And this whole triad that I have acquired has turned out contrary; having met with this calamity, we shall suffer bitterly.
t.1.148.14: Now that turn, the destroyer of our family, has come upon us: the food and one man must be given by me as the payment.
t.1.148.16: So I, deeply sunk in a vast ocean of sorrow that is hard to cross, will go today to the Rākṣasa together with these kinsmen of mine. Then that vile one will devour all of us together.
t.1.148.15: I have no wealth anywhere with which to buy a man, and in no way shall I be able to hand over one of my friends or kin. Nor do I see any means of deliverance from that demon.
